claims_used: The imported morphology contains separate bilateral pedicel, funiculus and arista bodies.
Each pedicel-funiculus-arista chain has three-axis joints and author mass, inertia, stiffness and damping.
The simplified meshes retain the author model's left-to-right reflection convention.
sources.implementation_effect: Fits collision proxies in each actual segment's local coordinates and adds zero mass so author body mass and inertia remain authoritative.

sources.title: NeuroMechFly 2.0, a framework for simulating embodied sensorimotor control in adult Drosophila
claims_used: The pinned FlyGym body is an articulated adult Drosophila sensorimotor model.
Its body and mesh assets are the morphology authority for this import.
sources.implementation_effect: Uses the author's articulated antennal bodies and local mesh coordinates instead of adding antennae to a generic body.

sources.title: NeuroMechFly, a neuromechanical model of adult Drosophila melanogaster
claims_used: The morphology originates in micro-CT anatomy of one adult female fly.
The model remains an engineered biomechanical reconstruction rather than a population anatomical distribution.
sources.implementation_effect: Preserves the imported segment mass and inertia and labels the proxy fit as a synthetic approximation.

sources.title: Distinct sensory representations of wind and near-field sound in the Drosophila brain
claims_used: Mechanical movement of the antennal receiver drives Johnston's-organ pathways.
Different Johnston's-organ populations distinguish oscillatory sound from sustained wind-like deflection.
sources.implementation_effect: Keeps actual antennal joint position, angular velocity and generalized load alongside contact force; it does not assign a measured cellular gain to synthetic solid contact.

sources.kind: project anatomical interface derived from MaleCNS annotations
claims_used: BODY807 already has bilateral pedicel, funiculus and arista joint position, angular velocity, generalized load and segment-contact channels.
Segment contact is an engineered projection to anatomically matched tactile or mechanosensory afferent cohorts.
sources.implementation_effect: Uses the existing CNS-only sensory route without adding source identity, object labels or a parallel controller input.

limits: The 95-percent mesh fits are synthetic collision approximations, not measured cuticle compliance, bristle placement or receptor geometry.
Triangle-record vertices weight the fit by mesh tessellation density.
MuJoCo contact force and author joint mechanics provide reciprocal physical coupling; they do not establish a biological receptor transfer function.
The 2 ms contact time constant is an engineered numerical compliance chosen to remain measurable by the current 1 kHz physical packet; it is not measured antennal stiffness or damping.
